posts.name: Kaercha

ChatGPT is not AI the way you think it is. It’s an LLM. It’s not intelligent. It doesn’t “know” things. It guesses what the next best word would be over and over again to illicit a positive response from the reader. It doesn’t have opinions. It doesn’t perform analysis. It literally tries to guess what words you find appealing, and that’s the end of it.

That’s not to say it isn’t a wonderful tool within its scope, but this isn’t its scope.

ChatGPT is only as good as it’s training inputs. The communities on reddit and here are predominantly casual players who do not have a good grasp of balance and do not play at a high level. Their opinions about what are good or bad are often wrong, or contextual to a certain setting. There’s only a small number of gamers playing at a high level, e.g. WF raiders, MDI, and AWC players, and their opinions are likely drowned out by the huge mass of casual-above average people, who might sometimes be correct but often miss nuance. ChatGPT doesn’t think or parse these kinds of issues, it just weights things based on its training inputs.

For another example, most League players are bronze->gold. There’s very few diamond+ players. If you just asked everyone what champion is OP in an unbiased way you’d probably get a weird conclusion like Garen is OP, even though no elite player who actually understands the game thinks that, because some champions are “newb killers”, usually simple archetypes who do well in low level play, but their deficiencies are exploitable by higher level players.

GPT-3.5 is awful with those things but GPT-4 can be good sometimes; for example I watched Rocky for the first time before it was set to leave Netflix a couple months ago, and even though it’s like everyone’s dad’s favorite movie and I had it pinned as the type of manly meathead movie that I wouldn’t enjoy, I thought it was a pretty good film and had a lot of thoughts about it and asked ChatGPT this question:

In the movie Rocky, the primary antagonist is named Apollo Creed, which is an odd name and obviously must have been chosen for a reason. I don’t remember whether I got this from Friedrich Nietzsche or Camille Paglia but I remember hearing that “Apollonian” was the opposite of “Dionysian” (or “chthonic” in Paglia’s terminology) and Apollonian was associated with the sky while Dionysian/chthonic was associated with the earth. The name of the protagonist of the movie isn’t “Dionysus” but it is “Rocky,” so it still has to do with the earth in a sense. Do you know whether the filmmakers had these concepts in mind when they made the story, or whether this is a common observation?

and ChatGPT said:

The names “Rocky” and “Apollo Creed” in the Rocky franchise might indeed evoke associations with the Apollonian and Dionysian dichotomy, but it’s not definitively known if this was an intentional choice by the filmmakers. The Apollonian and Dionysian dichotomy is a philosophical and literary concept, most famously discussed by Friedrich Nietzsche in “The Birth of Tragedy.” Apollo represents order, rationality, and clarity, while Dionysus represents chaos, emotion, and instinct. In Camille Paglia’s work, similar contrasts are examined using the terms “Apollonian” and “chthonic,” referring to sky and earth respectively.

Apollo Creed is an elite, polished boxer who follows a scientific approach to boxing. He’s disciplined, calculating, and operates under a spotlight of celebrity and media attention, akin to the sky deity Apollo who represents light, clarity, and order. Rocky Balboa, on the other hand, is a down-to-earth, almost primitive fighter who draws upon raw emotion and instinct, in line with Dionysian or chthonic attributes.

However, there’s no concrete evidence that suggests the filmmakers were deliberately invoking these archetypes when naming their characters. Sylvester Stallone, who wrote the screenplay, has spoken at length about the film’s inspirations, which primarily revolved around the idea of an underdog rising to the occasion. He hasn’t explicitly mentioned Nietzschean philosophy or similar concepts as an influence on the characters’ names or their traits.

That said, it wouldn’t be the first time that viewers have made deeper literary or philosophical connections with a film’s content than was originally intended by its creators. Such interpretations can add a layer of richness and complexity to the story, whether or not they were deliberately planned.

That’s a pretty good answer; obviously there’s no way for me to know if parts of it are actually true (i.e., that Sylvester Stallone never talked about this), but the analysis that sort of explores how there could be a connection seems really good—it’s better than what I could’ve come up with, because I wasn’t really even thinking about it that deeply.

GPT-4 is still pretty weak when it comes to giving accurate info about WoW (although it can search the internet now); IMO the best way to use it with WoW is to just like copy people’s content that you’re too lazy to read or listen to and then get ChatGPT to feed the info to you in more of a Q&A format.

I don’t remember if GPT-3.5 ever had internet access but GPT-4 can search the internet, although that functionality was temporarily disabled because people were using it to do things like get around paywalls.

News websites often grant bots a different level of access to their content than ordinary users because they need their pages to get indexed by search engines. There were already ways to take advantage of this before ChatGPT, like Firefox/Chrome addons that can disguise your browser as a Google web crawler which will get around many paywalls.

I have ChatGPT Plus and can use GPT-4, so I asked it the same question as the OP but prefaced it a request to search the internet:

and it said

In World of Warcraft, certain DPS specs have consistently shown strong performance in raids and Mythic+ content across various expansions. Here’s a summary of what I found:

Rogues (Subtlety and Outlaw Specializations): Rogues, particularly with the Subtlety specialization, have maintained a strong performance in both raiding and Mythic+ content. They offer high burst damage and good control abilities. The Outlaw specialization is also notable. Rogues almost always have at least one spec in the upper tiers of performance, and their utility and survivability make them a top-tier choice for melee DPS.

Mages (Fire and Frost Specializations): Mages, especially in the Fire and Frost specializations, are known for their strong burst damage and AoE capabilities. Frost Mage has been noted for consistent good performance over several patches.

Warlocks: Warlocks traditionally have at least one spec that ranks in the top DPS for any given raid, particularly since the Pandaria expansion. Their specs, like Affliction and Destruction, are known for sustained DPS and damage over time abilities.

Demon Hunters (Havoc Specialization): The Havoc specialization of Demon Hunters is known for high mobility and strong AoE damage. They have been in demand for several patches, particularly since the Antorus raid.

Hunters (Marksmanship and Beast Mastery Specializations): Marksmanship Hunters provide strong single-target and AoE damage with good mobility. Beast Mastery Hunters are noted for their ability to maintain full DPS while on the move and have solid utility, although they tend to be kept in a lower tier due to their freedom of movement.

Please note that the performance of DPS specs can vary with different patches and expansions, and players often need to adapt to the changes. Additionally, while I gathered this information from various sources, some specifics might be missing due to the limitations in accessing certain websites.
